text.p: These are the leading stories in. the Kenyan press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Britain is impressed with strides made by the Kenyan government in its political and economic reforms, says visiting British development minister, Baroness Lynda Chalker.

- More than 6.0 billion shillings will be spent to combat famine in several parts of Kenya, a spokesman for the Cereals and Produce Board said, adding that the food crisis was caused by drought, high cost of inputs, poor quality seeds and market instability as a result of liberalisation.
- Britain is to provide 1.7 billion shillings for a primary school education project.
- Britain's Chalker plays safe by declining to discuss the outcome of a 50-minute meeting with opposition leaders.

- Cotton farmers in Nyanza province have been advised by local government that marketing problems are temporary and they should not sell at low prices to middlemen but wait until ginneries are able to handle their produce.

- Management of Kaloleni Lime and Cement factories says they have met all environmental conditions for continued operations, after local people complained that pollution by heavy dust particles was damaging their crops.
- President Daniel arap Moi has called for countries fuelling conflict in Zaire to put an immediate stop to their actions.
- Tea farmers in Nandi district of western Kenya have called for the privatisation of leaf transport to curb corruption among local officials and improve the quality of the crop.
